catalog.description: The model catalog: every model by its ID, and every provider with its offerings of those models, built from models.dev.

properties.version: Version of the document's format. A reader accepts only the version it knows.
properties.source: Where the catalog was built from, such as "https://models.dev".
properties.generated: When the catalog was built. Every catalog lists it.
properties.spellings: How model names spell words of model IDs.
properties.labs: The labs that make the models, by lab ID.
properties.families: The model families, by family ID.

spellings.description: How model names spell words of model IDs: from the word in lower case to its spelling, such as "glm" to "GLM" and "minimax" to "MiniMax". A word not listed is capitalized.

lab.description: A lab that makes models, and its name, such as "ByteDance Seed" for "bytedance-seed".

properties.id: The lab's ID: the part of its models' IDs before the slash.
properties.name: The lab's display name.

family.description: A family of models, and its name, such as "Claude Opus" for "claude-opus".

properties.id: The family's ID, as a model's "family" names it.
properties.name: The family's display name.

model.description: A model as its lab describes it, apart from any provider, and the providers that offer it.

properties.lab: The ID of the lab that made the model: the part of the model's ID before the slash. A key of "labs".
properties.name: The model's display name.
properties.family: The ID of the model's family, a key of "families".
properties.type: The kind of model. Absent for a language model.
properties.released: When the model was released, as YYYY-MM-DD, or YYYY-MM when only the month is known. Every model lists it.
properties.updated: When the model was last updated, as YYYY-MM-DD, or YYYY-MM when only the month is known. Every model lists it.
properties.knowledge: The cutoff of the model's training data, as YYYY-MM or YYYY-MM-DD. Absent when not known.
properties.open_weights: Whether the model's weights are published.
properties.license: The license of the model's weights, such as "Apache-2.0".
properties.reasoning: Whether the model can reason before it answers.
properties.weights: Where the model's weights can be downloaded.
properties.links: Pages about the model, such as its model card.
properties.merged: IDs of models that models.dev lists apart, but that are tiers of this model, such as "openai/gpt-6-astra-fast". Their offerings are this model's variants.
properties.providers: IDs of the providers that offer the model, in order. Each lists an offering of it under the model's ID.

model_id.description: A model's ID: its lab's ID, a slash, and the model's ID at the lab, such as "anthropic/claude-opus-5-5", in lower-case letters, digits, "." and "-".

model_type.description: A kind of model other than a language model.

properties.tools: Whether the model can call tools.
properties.attachments: Whether a request can attach files, such as images or PDFs.
properties.structured_output: Whether the model can answer in a JSON schema the request gives. Absent when not known.
properties.temperature: Whether a request can set the sampling temperature. Absent when not known.
properties.input: The kinds of content the model takes.
properties.output: The kinds of content the model makes.

modality.description: A kind of content a model takes or makes.

properties.context: The context window, in tokens: the input and the output together.
properties.input: The most input tokens. Absent when the input may fill the context window.

weight.description: Where a model's weights can be downloaded.

properties.label: The link's text, such as "Hugging Face".
properties.format: The format of the weight files, such as "safetensors".
properties.quantization: The precision the weights are stored at, such as "fp8".

properties.label: The link's text.
properties.type: What the page is, such as "model_card", "paper", "blog" or "docs".

provider.description: A provider of models, and its offerings of them.

properties.name: The provider's display name.
properties.kind: Whether the provider is a lab or a gateway.
properties.endpoint: How to call the provider's API, unless an offering's "provider_options" names an endpoint of its own.
properties.doc: URL of the provider's documentation of its models.
properties.models: The provider's offerings, by model ID: the keys are keys of the catalog's "models".
properties.unlisted: The provider's models that are not in the catalog's "models", by the provider's model ID.

provider_kind.description: "lab" for a provider that serves the models it makes, "gateway" for one that serves models other labs make.

endpoint.description: How to call an API: its request format, its base URL, how it authenticates, and the environment variables it reads.

properties.format: The request format the API takes. Absent when not known.
properties.api: The API's base URL. It may hold environment variables as ${NAME}, such as ${AWS_REGION}, for a client to fill in.
properties.api_default: True when models.dev lists no base URL, and "api" is the one the provider's SDK uses by default.
properties.auth: How the API authenticates requests. Absent when not known.
properties.env: The environment variables the API reads: its keys and settings, such as "OPENAI_API_KEY" and "AWS_REGION".

format.description: An API's request format: how a client builds a request and reads the response. "openai-chat" is OpenAI's Chat Completions, "openai-responses" OpenAI's Responses, "anthropic-messages" Anthropic's Messages, "anthropic-vertex" Anthropic's Messages on Google Vertex AI, "gemini" Google's Gemini generateContent, and "bedrock-converse" Amazon Bedrock's Converse.

properties.scheme: How a request carries its credentials.
properties.header: The header that carries the API key, when "scheme" is "header", such as "x-api-key".

auth_scheme.description: How a request carries its credentials: "bearer" sends the API key as "Authorization: Bearer <key>", "header" sends it in the header "header" names, "aws" signs the request with AWS credentials, and "google" uses Google Cloud credentials.

offering.description: A model as one provider serves it: the model's facts at that provider, and how to call it there.

properties.name: The offering's display name: its model's name, or, for an unlisted offering, one made from its key. The provider's own name is "provider_options.name".
properties.family: The ID of the model's family, as the provider lists it.
properties.type: The kind of model. Absent for a language model.
properties.released: When the model was released, as the provider lists it: YYYY-MM-DD, or YYYY-MM when only the month is known. Every offering lists it.
properties.updated: When the model was last updated, as the provider lists it: YYYY-MM-DD, or YYYY-MM when only the month is known. Every offering lists it.
properties.knowledge: The cutoff of the model's training data, as the provider lists it: YYYY-MM or YYYY-MM-DD. Absent when not known.
properties.open_weights: Whether the model's weights are published.
properties.capabilities: What the model can do at this provider.
properties.limit: The model's token limits at this provider.
properties.reasoning: The reasoning controls the offering takes. Absent when the model does not reason.
properties.interleaved: Present when the provider streams reasoning between the parts of the answer.
properties.provider_options: How to call the model at this provider: the model ID to send, and any endpoint, request fields and headers.
properties.price: What a call costs. Absent when no price is listed.
properties.status: The offering's lifecycle state. Absent when it is active.
properties.variants: Tiers and modes the provider offers on top of the offering, by key: the tier, the mode, or both as "mode:tier", such as "fast" and "thinking:fast".
properties.aliases: Other model IDs the provider takes for this model, such as a dated snapshot or another region. They have no price or variants of their own.
properties.lab: For an unlisted offering, the ID of the lab its model ID names, if it names one.

provider_options.description: How to send a request to a provider: the model ID, and any endpoint, request fields and headers.

properties.name: The provider's own name for the model.
properties.endpoint: The API to call, in place of the provider's "endpoint".
properties.body: Fields to merge into the request body, object by object.
properties.headers: Headers to send with the request.

variant.description: A tier or a mode that an offering offers on top of its call, or both. Its "provider_options" change the offering's: an "id" or "endpoint" replaces the offering's, and "body" and "headers" merge into the offering's.

properties.name: The variant's display name: the offering's name and the variant's key, such as "GPT-6.1 Sol Ultrafast".
properties.tier: The service tier the variant runs in.
properties.mode: The mode the variant runs the model in, such as "thinking".
properties.provider_options: How the variant's call differs from the offering's.
properties.price: What a call costs. Absent when it costs what the offering costs.
properties.status: The variant's lifecycle state. Absent when it is active.

tier.description: A service tier other than the standard one, which trades price for speed.

status.description: A lifecycle state other than active.

reasoning.description: The reasoning controls an offering takes, and how its model reasons when a request sets none. A fact that is absent is not known.

properties.mandatory: Whether reasoning cannot be turned off. When it can, "efforts" starts with "none".
properties.default_enabled: Whether the model reasons when a request says nothing of reasoning.
properties.efforts: The effort levels the offering takes, lowest first. "none" turns reasoning off, whatever field the provider's API turns it off by: a client sends it as its API does, such as Anthropic's thinking type "disabled".
properties.default_effort: The effort the model reasons at when a request names none, one of "efforts".
properties.budget: The range of reasoning token budgets the offering takes. Absent when it takes none.

effort.description: A reasoning effort level. "none" turns reasoning off.

budget.description: A range of reasoning token budgets. A bound that is absent is not known.

interleaved.description: How a provider streams reasoning between the parts of an answer.

properties.field: The response field that carries the reasoning text, such as "reasoning_content". Absent when not known.

price.description: What a call costs, in US dollars per million tokens.

properties.cache_read: Per million input tokens read from the prompt cache.
properties.cache_write: Per million input tokens written to the prompt cache.
properties.reasoning: Per million reasoning tokens, when they cost other than output tokens.
properties.tiers: The rates of long prompts, from the shortest: each applies to prompts longer than its "above".

price_tier.description: The rates of prompts longer than "above" tokens, in US dollars per million tokens.

properties.above: The prompt length, in tokens, above which these rates apply.
properties.cache_read: Per million input tokens read from the prompt cache.
properties.cache_write: Per million input tokens written to the prompt cache.
properties.reasoning: Per million reasoning tokens, when they cost other than output tokens.
properties.estimated: True when no source lists these rates, and the catalog estimated them from the standard tier's rates of long prompts.
